 		<method name="_get_name" qualifiers="virtual const">
 			<return type="String" />
 			<description>
-				Virtual method which can be overridden to return the syntax highlighter name.
+				Virtual method which can be overridden to return the syntax highlighter name. This is a name that is displayed in the editor when selecting between syntax highlighters, e.g. [code]Markdown[/code].
body:
I don't think there's anywhere else where _"syntax highlighter name"_ would matter as an term worth remembering. You may as well merge the two sentences.
There's a bit of ambiguity because `e.g.` may refer to "name that is displayed", but also "syntax highlighters". Not sure how to solve that, but maybe:
```suggestion
				Virtual method which can be overridden to return the name that is displayed in the editor when selecting between syntax highlighters. For example:  [code]"Markdown"[/code].
```

body:
Minor thing. One time a contraction is used (_"don't"_) and the next it is not (_"will not"_).
This sentence is a bit repetitive. I am not sure how important it is to highlight (no pun intended) _"any syntax highlighting"_ here.
I've personally seen _"Script Editor"_ capitalized very often. I believe we capitalize docks & similar, and this is one such case.

```suggestion
				Files that do not have any supported syntax highlighter will be displayed without any highlighting.
				[b]Note:[/b] The user can manually override the syntax highlighting used for any open file, via the [b]Edit > Syntax Highlighter[/b] option at the top of the Script Editor.
```
Or similar
